A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SLUG and retain the same core method and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLIP unlearning measurements in Table 1 and Appendix D, plus generated-image and VLM response experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds SLUG results on UnlearnCanvas, quantitative VLM benchmarks, parameter-selection ablations, and adversarial evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same forget/retain losses, importance/alignment-based Pareto selection, and fixed-gradient single-layer update with binary search. Multi-identity composition and CLIP-encoder editing for diffusion and VLMs already appear in v2. v3's pseudocode and search details document the existing procedure without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: v3 adds UnlearnCanvas artistic-style and object erasure, MME/GQA/MMBench utility evaluation, and nudity/church unlearning with adversarial prompts. It also tests concept-arithmetic prompts and quantized deployment. Earlier identity, ImageNet-object, copyright, avocado-chair, and qualitative VLM scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The diffusion comparison expands beyond ESD and SalUn: Table 2 adds FMN, UCE, CA, SEOT, SPM, EDiff, and SHS using baseline results reported by UnlearnCanvas. Table 8 additionally includes SLD for nudity. The original CLIP comparator set and Figure 4 comparison are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include SDv1.5 UnlearnCanvas evaluation with UA/IRA/CRA, FID, resource metrics, and Gap Ratio; VLM evaluation with 100 images per identity across ten identities; and SDv1.4 attacks using 142 nudity and 50 church prompts. The newly introduced VLM FA formula is inconsistent: Equation 11 counts misidentifications, while Table 3 interprets lower FA as better.

E4.justification: v3 adds parameter-selection and multilayer ablations (Table 4), validation-size sensitivity (Table 5), related-class retention analysis (Table 7), concept-arithmetic and quantization tests, whitebox attacks (Table 8), and effectiveness/efficiency decomposition (Table 9). Existing multi-identity and layer-trajectory analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly provides mean-plus/minus summaries across ten identity-specific VLM outcomes, whereas v2 reports point estimates and averages without dispersion. The dispersion statistic is not explicitly labeled; neither additional repeated-seed runs nor increased replication is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 and v2 Table D1/v3 Table 6 retain their scores. Major additions include UnlearnCanvas style/object UA of 86.29%/75.43%, reported VLM FA averaging 2.8% after unlearning versus 99.50% for the original model, and UnlearnDiffAtk success rates of 90.32% for nudity and 80% for church. These are newly reported experiments, not demonstrated performance improvements over v2.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the Gap Ratio mathematical definition in Equation 10 and its normalized L1/L2 aggregation in Appendix D.4. The core unlearning formulation remains equivalent, and neither version provides an unlearning theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central single-layer efficiency claim remains, but v3 explicitly extends claimed capability to artistic styles and resistance to concept-arithmetic and quantization attacks. Its abstract replaces v2's assurance of privacy/legal compliance with comparable benchmark effectiveness at lower computational cost, while its conclusion emphasizes unresolved robustness.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive qualifications: complete erasure cannot be claimed, whitebox attacks remain effective, and theoretical understanding and relearning resistance are unresolved. It also discusses metric-weight sensitivity and new ablation tradeoffs. v2's detailed early-language/late-vision layer interpretation is removed; the avocado-chair collateral-damage explanation remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds Algorithms 1–3, search initialization and selection rules, ten search steps, validation subset sizes, an explicit UnlearnCanvas encoder, A100-40GB hardware, batch sizes, and per-layer parameter counts. These substantially expand reproducibility information. The code link already existed in v2, whose detailed data-access and dependency prose is shortened.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands positioning against diffusion-editing methods, including UCE, FMN, SPM, Diff-quickfix, MACE, and CRE. New discussion of EraseBench, concept-arithmetic attacks, quantization vulnerabilities, and adversarial recovery reframes robustness and side effects as central concerns beyond v2's emphasis on saliency-based unlearning.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites and condenses the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and discussion. It reorganizes the method subsections, replaces the long Discussion with separate ablation, limitations, and conclusion sections, and groups appendix material by model and purpose. The title and affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, rearranges Figure 2, combines learning-rate results within Table 1 cells, and redesigns VLM response figures. Numerous benchmark, ablation, robustness, and resource tables and image grids are added. Copyright figures and Pareto plots are relocated, while existing VLM examples are partly redisplayed.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v2's largely qualitative diffusion/VLM evidence with quantitative benchmarks, component ablations, and adversarial tests (Tables 2–4 and 8). Algorithms 1–3 and implementation details improve reproducibility, while explicit non-erasure and whitebox-vulnerability limitations temper earlier assurances. These resolve important evidential gaps. The gains outweigh reporting problems, including Equation 11's inconsistent FA definition and resource comparisons using different batch sizes for timing and memory in Appendix D.5.
